NDT training in Philadelphia: how it works for Philadelphia employers and technicians

NDT training in Philadelphia is delivered by Atlantis NDT as ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, taught live online or onsite at your refinery, shipyard, plant or shop under ASNT Level III oversight. Certification is issued by your employer under its written practice after training, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams, and an annual vision test.

Philadelphia is a harder NDT market to read than a single-industry town. Within an hour's drive of City Hall there is refining and fuel logistics on both banks of the Delaware, three nuclear stations, a revived commercial shipyard and a Navy engineering centre at the Navy Yard, a rotorcraft plant, one of the densest concentrations of pharmaceutical manufacturing in the country, and a transportation network of long-span bridges, rail viaducts and transit structures that all need periodic inspection. It is also a three-state market: a crew based in South Philadelphia can be working in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Delaware in the same week, under three different radiation regulators.

Atlantis NDT does not run a Philadelphia classroom. We serve Philadelphia employers and technicians by delivering theory live online and bringing practical training, exams and Level III documentation to your facility. This section adds what the overview above does not: the method-by-method map to Delaware Valley work, the certification path in order, how we schedule around outages, the regulators RT crews deal with, and the questions we are asked most. Request a Philadelphia training quote and we will usually reply within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Philadelphia

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for its method and level, then is aligned to the codes your Philadelphia customers invoke. Where a customer document such as a nuclear quality programme or Navy specification adds its own personnel requirements, we say so plainly rather than implying our course covers it.

MethodLevelsWhat Philadelphia employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic testing (UT)I, II, III prepWeld examination on refinery and terminal piping, thickness surveys on tanks and vessels, bridge weld and pin inspection, shipyard hull weldsLevel I: employer entry rules. Level II: Level I plus documented experience
Phased array UT (PAUT)II, III prepEncoded weld inspection on new construction at the shipyard, corrosion mapping on refinery and terminal equipment, nuclear-component examination under customer proceduresConventional UT Level II expected first
Time-of-flight diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThrough-wall sizing on thick pressure vessels and heavy structural weldsConventional UT Level II expected first
Radiographic testing (RT)I, II, III prepPiping and pressure welds at refineries, terminals and fabricators; castings; digital radiography in manufacturingSeparate state or NRC radiation safety qualification required before working with sources
Magnetic particle testing (MT)I, IIStructural steel welds on bridges and buildings, lifting equipment, forgings, ship structureNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II
Liquid penetrant testing (PT)I, IIStainless sanitary welds in pharmaceutical plants, aluminium and titanium aerospace parts, non-magnetic valve and pump componentsNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II
Visual testing (VT)I, IIWeld visual acceptance, borescope inspection of sanitary tubing and process systems, bridge and structure condition inspectionNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II
Eddy current testing (ET)I, IIHeat-exchanger and condenser tubing at refineries and power stations, aerospace surface crack detection, conductivity checksNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II

UT training covers sound propagation, probe selection, calibration on standard and job-specific blocks, DAC and TCG, angle-beam scanning of butt, fillet and nozzle welds, and flaw evaluation. For Philadelphia we add emphasis on thick-section structural welds, because bridge and shipyard work reward it. PAUT and TOFD cover focal laws, scan plans, encoded data collection and analysis for technicians already confident in conventional UT. RT covers exposure technique, image quality, film and digital interpretation and code acceptance. PT and VT carry more weight here than in most US cities because of the pharmaceutical and life-sciences sector, where sanitary weld quality is inspected visually and by borescope, and where surface methods on stainless steel are routine. ET suits technicians who want outage work on exchanger and condenser bundles. Level III candidates prepare for the ASNT Basic and Method exams through ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Philadelphia, step by step

Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Delaware do not license NDT technicians by method. Your employer certifies you, following a sequence that is identical whether you work for a refinery contractor in Delaware County or a fabricator in Northeast Philadelphia.

  1. Employer written practice. The company's document defines training hours, experience hours, exams, passing grades, vision requirements, recertification periods and the responsible Level III.
  2. Classroom training. You complete the formal training the practice requires for the method and level, live online, in an arranged cohort, or onsite. Recommended minimums are summarised in our training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised, documented hours in the method, working with certified personnel on real jobs.
  4. General exam. Written questions on the principles of the method.
  5. Specific exam. Written questions on your employer's procedures, equipment, codes and acceptance criteria, such as ASME Section V and VIII, B31.3, AWS D1.1 or AWS D1.5.
  6. Practical exam. Hands-on examination of specimens with known discontinuities, graded against a checklist. A Level III administers and grades all three exams.
  7. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated annually.
  8. Certification. Issued by the employer, signed by the responsible Level III, and kept on file for audit.
  9. Recertification. On the interval in the written practice, by re-examination or documented continued performance as the practice allows. A new employer recertifies you under its own practice.

Many nuclear-sector customers require ANSI/ASNT CP-189 instead of SNT-TC-1A; the steps are similar but the standard is mandatory rather than recommended. See SNT-TC-1A training and certification for more.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Philadelphia crews

Three delivery routes, described honestly:

  • Live online theory for the classroom hours, delivered by an instructor in real time, useful for technicians working rotating shifts at a terminal or on a transit contract. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility for groups: theory, practical and exams at your plant, yard or shop, using your equipment and specimens that match your work.
  • Blended: theory online, then a concentrated in-person practical and exam block. No credible scheme allows the practical exam to be done remotely.

Philadelphia scheduling has its own rhythm. Nuclear refuelling outages at stations in the region run on fixed cycles and absorb every qualified technician for weeks, so training before an outage is far more useful than training during one. Refinery and terminal maintenance clusters in the shoulder seasons, and bridge inspection work is busiest in the warmer months when access is easier. Pharmaceutical shutdowns are short and planned well in advance. Tell us your calendar and we will build training blocks around it. Ask about onsite training for your Philadelphia crew, or see corporate NDT training for multi-site programmes.

Where NDT technicians work in Philadelphia

Refining and fuel logistics. The large refinery complex in South Philadelphia closed after its 2019 fire, and the site is being redeveloped as a logistics and life-sciences district, but refining did not leave the Delaware Valley. Refineries across the river in Paulsboro, New Jersey, and in Delaware City, along with the Trainer refinery and terminals at Marcus Hook, keep mechanical-integrity work flowing. That work relies on UT thickness, PAUT corrosion mapping, RT of piping welds and ET of exchanger bundles, referenced to ASME Section V, B31.3 and owner-user inspection programmes.

Nuclear power. Limerick Generating Station in Montgomery County and Peach Bottom in York County, plus the Salem and Hope Creek stations across the river in New Jersey, create steady demand for UT, PAUT, VT and ET during outages. In-service inspection follows ASME Section XI, which points to CP-189 for personnel qualification, and suppliers work under 10 CFR 50 Appendix B quality programmes. The NRC's Region I office is in King of Prussia.

Shipbuilding and Navy engineering. Hanwha Philly Shipyard at the Navy Yard builds large commercial vessels, and the Navy Yard also hosts the Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division and the Navy's propeller foundry. Weld inspection on hull blocks, MT on structural details and UT on thick plate are the entry points.

Aerospace and manufacturing. Boeing's Ridley Park rotorcraft plant and its supply chain bring aerospace NDT, which is usually certified to NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A. We are honest that we do not train to NAS 410; SNT-TC-1A training still builds method knowledge, but aerospace employers will certify you under their own scheme.

Pharmaceutical and life sciences. Southeastern Pennsylvania and South Jersey host major drug and biologics manufacturing, where stainless sanitary piping is built to ASME BPE and inspected visually and by borescope, with PT on accessible welds.

Bridges, rail and utilities. The Delaware River bridges, Amtrak's Northeast Corridor, SEPTA infrastructure and PennDOT's bridge inventory all need weld and structure inspection; bridge steel welding is governed by AWS D1.5. Philadelphia Gas Works, the largest municipally owned gas utility in the US, operates pipelines and an LNG facility; pipeline welding references API 1104.

Radiography licensing across three states. Pennsylvania is an NRC Agreement State, so radioactive-source radiography is licensed by the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection's Bureau of Radiation Protection. New Jersey is also an Agreement State, regulated by the NJ Department of Environmental Protection. Delaware is not an Agreement State, so radioactive materials licensing there is handled by the NRC from its Region I office. Radiographers must meet the radiation safety training and certification rules of whichever jurisdiction the job falls under, in addition to SNT-TC-1A certification in RT. Our RT courses teach the method; they do not replace those radiation safety requirements.

What local employers ask for. Documented Level II in UT, MT or PT, clean annual vision records, experience with the specific code your contract names, and, for nuclear work, CP-189-compliant records. Some local employers also ask for AWS CWI, API 510 or 570, or ISO 9712; we do not train for those schemes. For pay context, see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Philadelphia NDT companies

Philadelphia inspection companies often serve customers across three sectors with three different expectations: a refinery wants SNT-TC-1A records, a nuclear supplier wants CP-189, and a pharmaceutical client wants validated visual inspection records. A single written practice that is vague about all three will fail the strictest audit. We review or write your NDT written practice so it covers the standard each customer requires, provide outsourced Level III services for exams and certifications, write method procedures aligned to your customers' codes, and audit your certification files before your customers do. Book a Level III consultation for your Philadelphia company. More background is at SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical NDT, our 3D simulator, lets trainees practise 12 methods across five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Philadelphia candidates that spans shipyard welding, refinery piping and aerospace components. It builds familiarity with set-up and scanning between sessions. It is practice only and does not replace the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

Programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and Level III sign-off for Atlantis cohorts, online and onsite.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Philadelphia

How do I get NDT certified in Philadelphia?

Join or be sponsored by an employer that performs NDT, complete the training and supervised experience its written practice requires, pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass a vision test. The employer then certifies you. Atlantis delivers the training and can provide Level III exam and certification support.

Can I take NDT training online in Pennsylvania?

The classroom portion, yes, where your employer's written practice accepts live online instruction. The practical training and practical exam must be done in person on real specimens.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

That depends on the training and experience hours your employer's written practice sets for UT Level I and Level II, and on how much documented experience you already hold. See the training requirements matrix for recommended minimums. Accumulating supervised experience usually takes longer than the classroom work.

Do I need a license for radiography in Pennsylvania?

Radioactive-source radiography in Pennsylvania is licensed by the Department of Environmental Protection, and radiographers must meet its radiation safety training and certification rules. That is separate from, and in addition to, SNT-TC-1A certification in RT. Jobs in New Jersey fall under the NJ DEP, and jobs in Delaware under the NRC.

What does NDT training cost in Philadelphia?

We quote on request. It depends on method, level, group size, delivery mode and whether exams and Level III support are included. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Philadelphia employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most common basis for employer certification across refining, fabrication, shipbuilding and infrastructure in the region. Nuclear customers often require CP-189, and aerospace employers usually certify to NAS 410. In every case, your training and experience records are what a new employer reviews.

Is there an NDT school in Philadelphia?

Local colleges have offered NDT programmes, and they are a sensible route for individuals starting from scratch. Atlantis serves a different need: employer cohorts trained online or onsite, and technicians whose employer needs Level III-backed exams and records.

Which methods matter most for pharmaceutical plants?

VT, including borescope inspection of sanitary welds, and PT on accessible stainless welds. Volumetric methods are used less often in that sector.

Can you train our crew onsite in the Delaware Valley?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your plant, yard or shop is our standard model for groups anywhere in southeastern Pennsylvania, South Jersey and northern Delaware.

Do you train for nuclear-sector NDT?

We deliver method training and can align written practices to CP-189. Nuclear owners and vendors also apply their own qualification programmes and performance-demonstration requirements, which remain their responsibility.

Do you offer CWI, API or ISO 9712 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Some Philadelphia employers ask for those credentials, which are earned through their own schemes.

Can my company outsource its Level III?

Yes. Many small Philadelphia NDT companies do. Ask about outsourced Level III support in Philadelphia.
